comparator.name: Art History
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official UvA study-programme page gives a complete 180-EC curriculum: ten 6-EC first-year components; a 60-EC second year combining five named 6-EC components, a 12-EC specialisation, a 12-EC excursion and 6 EC of free choice; and a third year with a 12-EC research seminar, 36 EC of free choice and a 12-EC bachelor thesis. Named bounded choice and free-choice space are represented at their published EC values without inventing course titles.

alternatives.labelRationale: This is a distinct, interest-supported route through the same UvA subject: modern art and museums are combined with film, visual culture, public communication and social theory. alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Eight courses (60 EC) differ in each direction: this route replaces historical, archaeological and literary contexts with television/social media, environment, film adaptation, communication and sociology. The change follows Leiden’s formally documented Arts, Media and Society direction and alters the academic centre of the 24-course curriculum.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest programme owns the six generator-eligible interests centred on art history, historical breadth, techniques, architecture and museums. The remaining six generator-eligible visual-culture, social-change, interpretation and art-society interests support one coherent contemporary art, media and society alternative. The two schedules differ by eight courses each way and satisfy the hard constraints. No independently evidenced third organising direction remains, so production stops at two.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both supply explicit academic-skills preparation; UCR PPD is broader than the programme-specific UvA course.
Both introduce Western art history and visual interpretation; UCR begins with the Renaissance rather than reproducing the full UvA survey.
Both analyse how cultural objects are made and interpreted through material and visual evidence; UCR approaches this through archaeology.
African Art & Heritage supplies a substantive non-European art-history and heritage perspective within the UvA global-art component.
UCR directly studies Renaissance painting, sculpture and architecture, covering a defined portion of the UvA Western-art sequence.

notes.text: The UvA programme provides a sustained 180-EC art-history sequence with visual analysis, techniques, Western and global art history, professional practice, excursions, specialist seminars, research and a bachelor thesis. UCR offers a smaller art-history and heritage sequence and adds relevant archaeology, history, media and cultural-analysis courses; it does not reproduce the full specialist sequence or dedicated art-history thesis.
